Claire: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel fallback roll, p99 latency spiked for a subset of small-concat requests. Not huge throughput impact but tail jumped ~120ms

Joel: saw that on the dashboard. p95 stable, p99 up from ~420ms to ~540ms, p999 noisy. Any obvious root cause?

Maria: I looked at the profiler. When kernel A fails we now route to kernel C which has ~30% worse init latency for short sequences because of a cold init path + extra memcpy. KV hit rate also dipped for a few prefixes.

Claire: exactly — pattern is tiny prompts (~8-32 tokens) where batching tries to fill microbatches, then kernel selection switches late and we pay a fallback penalty.

Sam: Can you paste the snippet of the fallback path? infra-bot logged the kernel handshake traces earlier.

infra-bot: deploy:kernel-fallback v3 -> v2 at 2026-03-17T21:45:12Z
infra-bot: trace: request_id=rq_8a3f, chosen_kernel=C, fallback_reason=kernel_failure, kernels_tried=[A,B,C]

Maria: profiler excerpt: 
```
# sample tail profile (short seq)
mean_exec(A)=6.2ms, cold_init(A)=1.1ms
mean_exec(B)=7.0ms, cold_init(B)=1.4ms
mean_exec(C)=8.5ms, cold_init(C)=12.0ms  # big memcpy + prewarm
KV_hit_rate_prefix=0.82 -> 0.65 during spike
```

Rik: That cold_init(C)=12ms is the culprit for p99. For small sequences that extra prewarm dominates. We need smarter routing or to bias scheduling to prefer kernels with lower cold_init when microbatching small seqs.

Joel: Also saw queue behavior — max_batch_tokens currently 1024, max_wait_ms=6. Under microburst load we observed batch sizes swing and queue phasing makes fallback timing align badly with kernel handshakes.

Claire: proposal: create a tiny_seq_policy that tweaks two things: (1) if estimated tokens_per_req < 64 and estimated_batch_size < 8 then reduce max_wait_ms to 3 (favor latency) and prefer kernel A/B; (2) when KV_hit_rate < 0.75 avoid kernel C unless no other kernel is healthy.

Sam: +1 to policy. Also suggest instrumenting a moving-window KV hit metric per router to avoid global noise. We should add a short-lived probe to prime KV for hot prefixes: on mismatch, send a best-effort background priming request (non-blocking) to populate cache.

Maria: I can add an experiment in runtime config. Example patch: 
```
routing_policies:
  tiny_seq_policy:
    max_wait_ms: 3
    max_batch_tokens: 256
    prefer_kernels: [A,B]
    kv_prime_on_miss: true
    kv_prime_ttl_ms: 200
```

Rik: Also let's run two A/B lanes for 1 hour: lane A = current defaults, lane B = tiny_seq_policy + kernel bias. Measure p95/p99, throughput delta, and KV hit delta. If p99 improves >30ms with <3% throughput loss we roll.

Claire: agreed. Action items:
- Maria: land routing experiment and enable infra logging of kernel choice + add kv_hit_ratio meter (1h window) (ETA: today EOD)
- Sam: add the background KV prime hook + make it opt-in (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- Joel & Rik: run A/B and collect p95/p99/throughput/KV metrics (start 02:30 UTC)

Joel: one more thought — also test bumping max_batch_tokens down to 512 for the tiny_seq_policy; that reduces packing and reduces chance of long wait buildup. Might help tail.

Claire: good call. Maria include that as variant B1 (512) vs B2 (256).

Sam: will monitor error budgets. if p99 degradation >100ms rollback automatically via rollout policy.

Rik: logging note — include a small tag `microbatch_cause` in traces: values {kv_miss, kernel_fallback, queue_delay} so we can slice p99 by cause.

Claire: perfect. Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the 1h A/B run and share a short postmortem. :thumbsup:
